synopsis: 29 CFR 1926.602(a)(9)(ii), alongside 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4), is in force for US construction [f2762]. When a machine’s rear view is obstructed, these rules require a reverse signal alarm audible above surrounding noise, or an observer [f15505, f2763, f2764]. Chapter 3 also reports that interpretations allow camera and radar alternatives [f2763]. The rules prescribe neither a numeric range nor automatic braking, leaving those parameters unspecified by these provisions for collision-mitigation validation planning [f2765].

relations.note: Both require a reverse alarm or observer when the rear view is obstructed.
Both state that the reverse alarm must be audible above surrounding noise.
Specifies the audibility requirement for the alarm option.
Adds that interpretations allow camera and radar alternatives.
Clarifies that the stated obligations include neither numeric range nor automatic braking.
